subject: Post-demo econ check & startup incentive path for Parcella
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara@parcella.co>, Devin Marshall <devin@parcella.co>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo econ check & startup incentive path for Parcella

Hi Sara / Devin,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciated seeing how Parcella routes pickup volumes and the latency targets you mentioned. Quick recap and asks so we can put together a startup offer and committed-path pricing: 

- Volumes: you said production peak of ~10M tokens/day with average ~3M tokens/day and expected growth to ~25M tokens/day over 6–9 months. Please flag if those numbers change.
- Budget band: you mentioned an initial monthly cloud budget target of $10k–$25k while you validate the feature. Confirm whether that is net of infra and embedding costs or a spend target specific to generation tokens.
- Unit economics target: what is the internal target $/1M tokens we should aim for with a committed discount (e.g., $/1M tokens after discount)? If you don’t have a target, list what would make sense (e.g., below $150 / 1M).
- Startup program: you indicated Parcella recently closed seed — if you can share the lead investor and company incorporation date we’ll verify eligibility and prepare the starter credit + founder credit proposal.

Next steps I propose: I’ll put together two price paths — a modest committed-use discount for a 6–12 month minimum commitment, and a startup promotion with credit + reduced tiers for the first 3 months. Ben (cc) will review the economics and Laura can sign off for an exception if we need a custom multi-year structure.

Attachments: parcella-demo-notes.pdf (call notes), startup-discount-worksheet.xlsx (blank for you to fill volumes).

Could you reply with: 1) confirm the 3 numbers above (peak/avg/growth), 2) your target $/1M tokens or a range, and 3) incorporation date & lead investor for startup eligibility?

Thanks — I’ll target a draft offer by Tuesday.

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0183

From: Devin Marshall <devin@parcella.co>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Nguyen <sara@parcella.co>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 08:09:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo econ check & startup incentive path for Parcella

Thanks Hannah — great demo, we left with a clear picture. Quick answers below and a couple questions: 

On volumes (confirming):
- avg ~3M tokens/day (production baseline)
- peak ~10M tokens/day (observed during heavy routing tests)
- growth to ~25M tokens/day within 6–9 months if pilot goes well

Budget: the $10k–$25k monthly band is our near-term cap for model inference only (generation tokens). Embeddings and storage will be handled separately by another line item.

Target unit economics: we don’t have an internal benchmarking number yet — to be candid, anything below $120 / 1M tokens would make deployment economics attractive for our use case.

Startup eligibility: Parcella incorporated 2025-08-09. Lead investor is BlueHarbor Capital (seed). Happy to share the cap table if needed — would prefer an NDA before that.

Questions:
1) Does your definition of "tokens" include prompt + response tokens or only generated (response) tokens? We want to ensure we model costs correctly.
2) For the committed discount path, do you require a dollar-minimum commitment or can it be tokens/month with a lookback?

Appreciate the quick follow-up. We uploaded the filled worksheet (startup-discount-worksheet.xlsx) to the drive link below.

Thanks,
Devin
Devin Marshall
Head of ML, Parcella
devin@parcella.co

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo econ check & startup incentive path for Parcella

Forwarding Parcella thread — Devin confirmed volumes and stated a target below $120 / 1M tokens if we can get to it with a 6–12 month committed path. They’re seed (2025-08-09) with lead BlueHarbor — qualifies for startup program.

Proposed quick offer to approve: 
- Starter package: $50k credit applied over first 8 weeks, plus an initial 20% off retail token price for first 3 months.
- Committed path: 6 month commit of $12k/month (pre-discount) with stepped discounts to give an effective price of ~$100 / 1M tokens at 25M/day projected usage (this is conservative math, final numbers in spreadsheet).

Attachments: attached my annotated starter worksheet (startup-discount-worksheet.xlsx).

Laura / Hannah — can we approve a one-time founder credit + the proposed 20% starter discount? If we need a multi-year carve (2-year with lower $/1M), I suggest we route to commercial for review.

Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Growth, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo econ check & startup incentive path for Parcella

Thanks Devin — that’s perfect, and congrats on the seed close. Quick answers to your two questions and next steps: 

1) Token definition: Redwood counts both prompt + response tokens for billing. For the committed path we can provide an itemized example showing prompt vs response breakdown (we typically show a 60/40 split for routing prompts vs generated text in this class of workload).
2) Commitment shape: we can accept either a dollar-minimum commit or a tokens/month commitment with a 30-day lookback and true-up. If you prefer tokens/month we’ll map to an equivalent $ floor to simplify accounting.

Approved for the starter package: Ben / Laura approved a one-time founder credit and a 20% starter discount applied for the first 90 days. I’ll send the formal pricing summary + DocuSign by EOD and include the committed-path term sheet for your review (6 or 12 month options).

Next steps for Parcella:
- Hannah to send pricing summary + DocuSign link (today)
- Devin to confirm whether you want the 6- or 12-month committed path for pricing calculations and sign the DocuSign
- Ben to confirm any multi-year commercial escalation if Parcella requests 2-year structure

Drive link (worksheet): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1_parcella_startup_workbook
DocuSign preview: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/parcel-sign-2147

Talk soon — I’ll share the formal doc shortly.

Best,
Hannah
